about: Extra coach notes and one client program used only by the expanded eval set. The seeded demo still ships the five demo articles. These are made up for a fictional gym.

articles.title: Late cancel and no show policy
articles.body:
Cancel at least 12 hours before your session and nothing is charged. You can cancel from the Book tab.

A late cancel inside 12 hours counts as a used session. A no show also counts as a used session.

If you are running late, the session still ends at the booked time. After 15 minutes the slot is released.

articles.title: Warm up routine
articles.body:
Start every session with 5 minutes on the bike or the rower at an easy pace.

Then do two ramp sets of your first lift. Use half the working weight for the first ramp set and three quarters for the second.

Save long static stretching for after the session. Before lifting, keep stretches short and moving.

articles.title: Rest between sets
articles.body:
Rest 2 to 3 minutes between sets of big lifts like squats, deadlifts, bench press, and rows.

Rest 60 to 90 seconds between sets of accessory exercises like curls, raises, and lunges.

The Log tab has a rest timer. It starts when you mark a set done.

articles.title: When to add weight
articles.body:
Add weight when you finish every set at the top of the rep range with two reps left in the tank.

Go up 5 pounds on upper body lifts and 10 pounds on lower body lifts the next session.

If you miss reps two sessions in a row, stay at that weight for one more week before going up again.

articles.title: Missed workouts
articles.body:
If you miss a workout, do it on your next training day and push the rest of the week back by one day. Do not double up two workouts in one day.

If you miss more than a week, restart the current week from day one.

articles.title: Logging your workout
articles.body:
Open the Log tab and tap the exercise. Enter the weight and reps for each set, then tap Done.

Logging works without a signal. Your sets are saved on the phone and sync when you are back online.

You can skip a workout from the Log tab. Add a short reason so your coach can see why.

articles.title: Gym hours
articles.body:
The gym is open 6 am to 9 pm on weekdays and 8 am to 2 pm on Saturday and Sunday.

The gym is closed on public holidays. Holiday closures are posted on the front door a week ahead.

articles.title: Equipment is taken
articles.body:
If the squat rack is taken, do goblet squats or the leg press for that day.

If the bench is taken, use dumbbells on the floor or an incline bench.

Write the change in the exercise note when you log it so your coach knows what you did.

articles.title: Session packs
articles.body:
Sessions are sold in packs of 5 or 10. A pack expires 90 days after you buy it and unused sessions do not roll over.

You can freeze a pack once for up to 30 days. Ask at the front desk to start a freeze.

articles.title: What to bring
articles.body:
Bring a water bottle, a small towel, and flat shoes. Chalk is at the front desk.

Each session runs 45 minutes. Arrive 5 minutes early so you can start your warm up on time.

articles.title: What RPE means
articles.body:
RPE is how hard a set felt on a scale of 1 to 10. RPE 8 means you had two reps left. RPE 10 means you had none left.

Most working sets in your program should land at RPE 7 or 8.

program.name: Foundation 3-day
program.text:
Program: Foundation 3-day
Day 1: Lower A
Back squat. 3 sets of 8 reps. Brace before you descend.
Romanian deadlift. 3 sets of 8 reps. Soft knees, flat back.
Walking lunge. 2 sets of 10 reps. Short steps.
Day 2: Upper
Bench press. 3 sets of 8 reps. Feet planted.
Barbell row. 3 sets of 8 reps. Pause at the hip.
Overhead press. 3 sets of 6 reps. Ribs down.
Day 3: Full body
Goblet squat. 3 sets of 10 reps. Elbows inside the knees.
Push up. 3 sets of 8 reps. Body in one line.
Hip hinge. 3 sets of 10 reps. Light and smooth.
